item.title: Kaike Onsen: A Seaside Hot Spring Facing Mount Daisen — Guide
item.description: Kaike Onsen, on the coast near Yonago just over the border from Matsue, is unusual: its saline, mineral-rich hot water was discovered in the late nineteenth century bubbling up in the shallows of the sea itself. Today it is a seaside resort where a line of large ryokan and hotels faces a long sandy beach on the Sea of Japan, so bathers can soak looking straight out over the water at sunset.

item.title: Atami Onsen: The Classic Seaside Hot Spring Resort — Guide
item.description: Atami, meaning ‘hot sea’, is one of Japan’s most famous hot spring resorts, its salty, mineral-rich waters used for over a thousand years and beloved by shoguns, writers and honeymooners across the centuries. The town tumbles down a steep hillside to a palm-lined bay, mixing grand historic ryokan and seaside baths with the retro charm of its Showa-era heyday, and after years of decline it is enjoying a stylish revival, with renovated inns, cafes and a young crowd drawn by the 40-minute Shinkansen hop from Tokyo.
